areas.why: ISA 240 presumption not rebutted: cash-handling taproom under a dominant owner with expressed willingness to run personal items through the company. The takings series has three missing weeks in peak season (no ledger entry and no bank deposit for c. 8 May, 15 May, 15 Aug; ~33k gross, above PM), duplicated week labels, and weekly combined 'CARD/CASH DEPOSIT' credits although the card terminal supposedly settles daily. Trade sales are clean (sequential CVB-2025-1001..1661, no gaps, no credit notes, no manual revenue entries), so trade cut-off is only elevated in substance.

Trade debtors rose from 75,935 to 210,658, but every one of the 74 open invoices at 31/12 was received in full by 2 Mar 2026 (B26 BACS credits total exactly 210,657.86) and all opening debtors were received in 2025. No credit notes, no unmatched receipts; ageing all <60 days. Other debtors are nil, which is itself wrong (director's personal spend should sit there).

No written approval policy (N14); Kate both posts and approves 384 of 494 purchase invoices and Dan approved an invoice for his own house (PI-000494). Seventeen 'monthly' alcohol duty returns were posted for twelve months, including four in December (78,870 unpaid at YE), which needs agreeing to HMRC's duty account; 'Valley Cleaning Services' invoices staff pizza nights and customer tasting evenings coded to entertaining. Year-end creditors 155,283 all cleared by 2 Mar 2026 and opening creditors 64,983 cleared in Jan 2025, so existence is lower risk than classification/completeness.

Kate runs payroll from the rota and approves the payroll journal herself (PR-000001..12 approvedBy kate.office); Dan only checks the total. Bank salary lines agree to the 18 named employees and the one leaver (Marcus, E004) was last paid 28 Oct, so no ghost/leaver issue in the data, but gross pay is identical every month Jan-Oct (46,150) despite a rota-driven, seasonal taproom, and Rosie Crossley (related party, 20 h/week) is paid 1,924 net/month, more than most full-time staff (e.g. 1,480). N7 says 18 on payroll at YE; bank shows 17.

Register has never been audited or physically verified (first audit, compiled PY). Only addition is two fermenters 96,000 net (PI-000493, paid B25-00942) - above PM. Depreciation was posted as an unchanged monthly template (5,900) all year, so the fermenters were not depreciated from August; the canning line runs two days a week (N3), an impairment indicator for the largest asset class (P&M 352,000).

Ledger 1200 agrees to the statement at 31/12 (-130,893) and every statement line matches a ledger posting (salaries match in aggregate per payroll run). But the account was overdrawn on 108 days, continuously from 12 Sep 2025 to 9 Feb 2026 with a peak of -161,323, whereas the bank's letter refers to four days of unarranged overdraft in September: either an arranged facility exists that is not in the file or the letter is incomplete. Cash in hand 1,500 is unchanged all year despite weekly cash takings. Q1 2026 statement ends 2 Mar and contains no takings, salaries, rent or loan DD.

Dan's home kitchen (Hebden Kitchen Studio, '14 Birchcliffe Road', 10,080 gross) was approved by Dan, coded to equipment maintenance 7700 with 1,680 input VAT reclaimed, paid by the company (B25-00787), and the director's loan account 2310 shows nil all year: a director's advance above the s.197 10,000 threshold, undisclosed, with BIK and VAT consequences. Rosie Crossley's pay is not on the 'same as anyone' terms claimed. Kate's reaction (N11) points to possible further items.

Owner-manager with unlimited posting/approval rights, a covenant test on these accounts (incentive), a PY loss turning into a profit while he says margins were squeezed (GP 46.8% to 50.4%), and an inconsistent account of who did the stock count. The only material manual entry is the round-sum stock uplift MJ-000016 (+56,000 in round thousands, posted 21 Jan 2026, approved by Dan). A Xero bank rule posts all loan interest (36,000) to bank charges; VAT transfer journals MJ-000010/MJ-000014 do not agree to the ledger; Hill & Co's year-end journals are not yet in the ledger (no hill.accts postings at all).

Covenants (N5) recomputed from the TB with the 36,000 interest reclassified out of bank charges: EBITDA ~146k, interest cover 4.1x, net debt/EBITDA 3.41x against a 4.0x limit, headroom ~21.5k of EBITDA, which is below PM; an unrecorded audit fee or a stock overstatement above ~22k breaches it. FY2024 (compiled) would have failed both tests (EBITDA 58k vs interest 34.5k). The account has been in overdraft since 12 Sep 2025, and the bank wants audited accounts and a compliance certificate by 30 June.

Stock 234,000 (7.8x materiality), counted without the auditor on 2 Jan on paper sheets by Dan with a contradictory account of who helped (N8), WIP valued 'by rule of thumb', posted as a round-sum journal (MJ-000016) three weeks after year end. The 56,000 increase drives the profit swing and covenant headroom and contradicts the margin squeeze in N3. Opening stock 178,000 was 'Dan's figure' with no count sheets.

First audit; FY2024 compiled, not audited (N2, N15). Opening stock 178,000 is unverified (PY-HILL-01) and flows straight into 2025 cost of sales. The opening loan of 600,000 is the full drawdown although repayments started in 2024 and 34,500 was booked as interest (PY-HILL-02), so capital/interest in FY2024 is likely misallocated. Opening debtors (75,935), creditors (64,983) and the VAT liability (19,000, B25-00077) are already cleared by 2025 cash.

Ledger VAT for 2025 is ~182.5k net payable but returns paid/claimed total ~103.8k: the Q1 transfer agrees to the ledger, but the Q2 return claimed a 9,421 repayment (received B25-00780) against ledger Q2 net payable 44,739, Q3 transferred 54,876 against 24,575, and Q4 was settled at 4,138 (B26-00096) against 59,013. About 78.7k of net output VAT sits in 2200/2201 undeclared, which is above materiality and carries a penalty/interest provision and cash consequences. Non-business input VAT was also reclaimed on PI-000494 and on customer entertaining (S020 tasting evenings).

Accruals of 6,200 are identical at the start and end of the year with no postings at all; there is no audit fee (7601 nil, no Thornbury invoice), no loan interest accrual, no holiday pay, no corporation tax account or charge, and no provision for VAT/duty penalties. With covenant headroom below PM, completeness matters more than size suggests.

The subsequent-events window must cover the bank's 30 June deadline, VAT/duty regularisation with HMRC and the overdraft position. The Q1 2026 statement provided appears partial (ends 2 Mar, has no takings, payroll, rent or loan DD), and alcohol duty compliance (rate change Feb 2025, 17 returns) falls under ISA 250.
